newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-SWISS INVESTOR WANTS MAJORITY IN WINTERTHUR.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-SWISS INVESTOR WANTS MAJORITY IN WINTERTHUR.

text.p: Swiss investment group BZ Trust, whose stake of at least 18 percent in insurer Winterthur has fueled takeover speculation, said its long-term aim was to acquire a majority holding in the globally-active insurance company.

BZ Trust, run by shareholder activist Martin Ebner, said it believed the investment was smart because Winterthur might be taken over in future by bank Credit Suisse Group or merge with a foreign partner.
Winterthur declined to say how much of its shares were now held by Ebner's group and dismissed speculation of an impending takeover from any side.
"We want to remain independent," Winterthur spokeswoman Anna-Marie Kappeler told reporters.

Ebner's interest in Winterthur has been public since May, when the insurer announced that BZ held a stake of 14.5 percent, making it its biggest shareholder by far, ahead of Swiss Reinsurance Co with nearly five percent.

"We later informed Winterthur's management that we are seeking a stake of over 50 percent in the long-term," BZ Trust said in a letter to shareholders in the group's listed investment funds, which have the stakes in the Swiss insurer.
Ebner announced in June that he had raised his Winterthur share from 14.5 percent to 18.3 percent, with about another five percent in the hands of customers of his BZ Bank.
But he declined at the time to say whether he was buying more of the insurer, whose shares have risen powerfully this year, especially since Ebner's interest became public.

Winterthur registered shares have been the best performer on the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) this year, surging 95 percent from 774 Swiss francs at the start of 1997 to a Friday close of 1,515 francs.
The share rose 1.9 percent in the past week in an overall weak market.
Winterthur is a leading European direct life and non-life insurer whose 1996 net profit rose 21 percent to 506.7 million Swiss francs on gross premiums of 25.9 billion Swiss francs, up 16 percent.

Ebner is Switzerland's most controversial professional investor after a drawn-out fight with management at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) over how to raise profitability at the country's biggest bank group.
In the letter to shareholders, BZ outlined three scenarios that it said justified a large holding in Winterthur.
BZ said if it succeeded in acquiring a majority stake, Winterthur management would have backing for speedier implementation of a more focused business strategy adopted in 1992.
"It would not be surprising if (Winterthur) profits doubled in a fairly short time," BZ wrote.
A second scenario would see Winterthur's board agree to a takeover offer from CS Holding, which would offer its shares as payment.
This would make BZ a significant shareholder in what might then be Switzerland's biggest bank and financial group, whose capitalisation BZ forecast at around 560 billion Swiss francs.
The third scenario would be if Winterthur allied itself or merged with a strong foreign partner offering complementary geographical presence and market share.
"In this case, former Winterthur shareholders might be part of a new insurance holding company that would be one of the strongest in the world," BZ wrote.
At Winterthur, spokeswoman Kappeler said BZ's letter was a statement of intent and that the group was still a long way from its goal of 50 percent or more.
"In this sense, we are not very preoccupied with the matter," she said.
Winterthur statutes limit any single shareholder or group of allied shareholders to five percent of voting rights regardless of the size of a stake, Kappeler noted.
